accuracy.evidence: The routine matches UK fire and rescue advice for families (GOV.UK Fire Kills escape plan; London Fire Brigade fire safety for children): a smoke alarm means get out, do not hide, keep low under smoke where the air is cleaner, do not stop for valuables or pets, go to an agreed meeting point, never go back in, and call 999 once out, asking for Fire and giving the address. The 999 operator's first question really is which service. Placement follows the PSHE Association Programme of Study 2020 KS1 (keeping safe at home, what to do in an emergency, calling 999). The adult text notes 911 and 112 for other countries and 111 as the NHS non-urgent line. Parameterised answers n-k and n+k stay positive whole numbers at every corner (p2 4-6 minus 1-3, m5, p4, m7).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented child behaviours in fires named in the adult text: hiding under a bed or in a cupboard (scene 1 'Hide under the bed' refusal, predict 1, m2, challenge 'hide'), stopping for toys (teddy/tablet on the floor reset the crawl, 'Find my toys first' card, m8, challenge 'toys'), standing tall in smoke (Walk tall route coughs and resets, predict 2, p3, m9, challenge 'tall'), waiting next to the house or hiding in a shed (window and shed spots refused, predict 3, p5, challenge 'close'/'shed'), going back in for a pet (Kitty cards, predict 4, m1, m4, challenge 'back') and not knowing the number (keypad refuses non-9s, m3, challenge 'number').

lab_distinct.evidence: flaggetout is built on escape mechanics specific to a house fire: a smoke layer whose bottom edge is a live boundary for the dragged child, floor objects that reset the escape, a meeting-place drop target with too-close and hidden decoys, a stay-out decision with a pet inside, and a working 999 keypad followed by the operator's two questions. 211 Rules that keep us safe (flagsafe) is a broad everyday-rules lab and 489 Using electricity safely (flagzap) is about plugs and water; flagfire (996) is a Great Fire of London reading lab. Lab shingle similarity is under 30% against every flag_*.js (lab_distinct gate passes).

lab_teaches.evidence: Each rule is discovered by trying it: hiding or fetching toys after the beep is refused with the reason, dragging the child into the grey layer gives 'Cough! Smoke is up high' and sends them back, touching the teddy says toys can be bought again, dropping Gran by the window says heat and smoke come out, 'Run back in for Kitty' is refused, and a wrong key names the digit and says three nines. The done messages restate the rule only after the scene has shown it, and the operator's 'Which service?' teaches the call script by doing it.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Hiding under my bed' (the lab refuses hiding and explains smoke gets in), 'Up high, near the ceiling' (the smoke layer fills the top and coughs the child back), 'Yes, I am out now' (the window spot is refused as too close) and 'Yes, quickly' for going back in for Kitty (that card is refused and a firefighter is told instead).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions whose wrong options carry nine distinct slip messages: hide (smoke gets in, firefighters cannot find you), toys (things can be bought again), look (do not look for the fire), tall (smoke rises, clean air near the floor), back (never go back in, tell a firefighter), close (heat and smoke come out), shed (nobody knows you are safe), number (three nines) and meaning (the beep is a warning, get out now).

readability.evidence: Kid text uses very short sentences and concrete words (beep, smoke, low, floor, meeting place) and passes the kid readability limit in validate_lessons; lab cards are four to six words; prompts for 4 to 5 year olds avoid abstract words, and the adult text uses the precise terms (smoke alarm, meeting place, 999, emergency services) within the adult limit.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph gives one action and its reason; adult paragraphs give the curriculum placement, why smoke and low air matter, the named mistakes with a calm-practice tip, and what the lab does. No content gate filler matches; lab text is instruction or feedback only.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360x640 screenshots in dark and light: the four first-move cards sit in a 2x2 grid with two-line labels, the smoke layer and 'clean air down low' labels are readable, the door, toys and child are separate, the family tiles no longer overlap at 360 px (width-based spacing), the 3x4 keypad keys are about 84 px wide, and the young-mode buttons below are 56 px tall. walk.cjs passed on iPhone 13 and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin (tap alarm, the four first moves, crawl low / walk tall / stop for teddy, pick a person then a place, the four Kitty cards, Press 9/1/0 and the operator answers). The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each scene description and feedback, the challenge uses role=status live feedback, wrong cards show a ✗ and right ones a ✓ as well as colour, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found nothing in light or dark on desktop or phone.
